accepted_findings: The revised protocol implements the user-authorized use of train curves and full val for training length; val never enters gradients, history normalization or target normalization.
R20 and R21 are independently constructed from the same SHA-bound A06 backbone and exact array equality is checked before data-driven training; R21 starts at lambda zero.
The single Torch effective_stiffness property feeds the RHS, same-stage tangent, linear path and closure export. R21 lambda remains in the complete three-GN/history-reset/future gradient path.
Both groups use continuous fresh Adam state, six full-train weighted gradient batches per committed update, common clipping norm and fixed projection of finite lambda to log(0.5)..log(2).

Full val monitoring uses the same masked 1 s/3 s event-equal target definition at 5 ms, 107-event weights and immutable train scales. Failed batches yield null full objectives and do not select checkpoints.

Separate strict-minimum checkpoint selection and common meaningful-improvement patience are correctly distinguished; exact ties retain the earliest checkpoint; an invalid active check resets patience.

A numerical training failure rolls back the incomplete update, retains a prior valid best checkpoint when available, and permits the other group to continue under the original schedule. Actual and selected update counts are preserved.
Final scoring executes both complete train and val cohorts at 2.5/1.25 ms regardless of RMSE, with one-time per-step individual isolation only after a batch exception and within the declared budget.

Frozen checkpoint export folds the effective stiffness into a fixed model, preserves the explicit three-GN/history-scale contract, and uses a restricted weights-only loader in the separately registered test path.
Terminal 1 s/3 s objectives use existing prediction arrays and fixed train scales; they are explicitly step-specific and retain null values when the implementation numerical qualification is not met.

The operation limits cover two 80-update fits, sixteen complete val checks and worst-case full train/val isolation. All 38 local bindings and all 60 inherited external scorer source bindings matched during review.

Optimization evidence is explicitly scoped to fixed Adam configuration, per-update loss/gradient/projection traces and full parameter snapshots at validation checks; no saved Adam-moment or resume contract is claimed.

engineering_evidence.coordinator_report: 69 core tests and 2 validation-selection tests passed; stiffness full-chain directional gradient relative error reported as 3.87e-7

boundaries: This review approves the exact fit plan only. It is a scientific source review and does not perform an operator approval, loop transition or scientific execution.
The final full test=76 evaluation is mandatory reporting under a separately registered zero-fit stage bound to both final selected checkpoints; no test payload is authorized by this fit review.
Val is a selection population in this round. The historically exposed test roster is a fixed comparison benchmark, not independent confirmation.
Early stopping is not proof of convergence. Boundary hits, numerical failures, invalid metrics, lost equal training exposure and fallback endpoints must remain explicit.
A separately registered arithmetic audit of new saved outputs must verify full trajectory/stability metrics, paired differences, failure lists and coverage before final scientific conclusions.
KEEP_BASELINE remains in force. This review grants no promotion, deployment change, extra training, harmonic search, renewed consumed scope or post-test model revision.
